ov: A huge, mostly plant-eating bear of northern forests, mountains and tundra, and one of the largest land carnivores alive. Grizzlies and Kodiak bears are brown bears too.

why.h: It dens up for the winter and lives off its fat, but it isn’t a full hibernator and can be woken easily.

rg: Northern North America, Europe and Asia. It lives in a wider range of habitats than any other bear, with small, fragmented populations left in western Europe.
df: Mostly grass, roots, berries and nuts, plus insects, fish such as salmon, and mammals from rodents up to moose.

cf.tip: Same species: “grizzly” is the name for inland North American brown bears. Every grizzly is a brown bear, but not every brown bear is a grizzly.
Go by shape, not colour: a brown bear has a muscular shoulder hump; a black bear has none.

fx: It can put on up to 180 kg of fat between summer and autumn to see it through the winter.
notes: why.h repeats the existing fact ("Does not truly hibernate"); keep one or the other, or rewrite the animals.js fact. Did not add an et note: brown bear meat is eaten, but I found no source in the checked text.
